messages:
kevin: thinking about per-org rate policy — we need RPM/TPM + concurrency caps, but want predictable UX for customers.
tara: do we mean RPM (requests/min) + TPM (tokens/min) or are we conflating terms? :thinking:
maria: want a hard concurrency cap per org so they can't spin up huge parallel requests and blow quota.
alex: +1 on concurrency. But curious: how do we handle short bursts? ex: burst for a worker pool that polls every 10s.
kevin: proposal sketch: sliding-window RPM for steady-state, token-bucket for controlled bursts, plus absolute concurrency limit. fallback to lower tier model when exceeded.
jen: console UX: need clear indicators — "throttled due to RPM" vs "in-flight concurrency" — and a rollout toggle for grace credits.
infra-bot: perf note: enforcing concurrency at edge vs at router changes observed p95 by ~30ms; edge enforcement cheaper but harder to aggregate metrics.
maria: can we offer ephemeral burst credits that decay over 24h? customers like buffer for migrations.
alex: care about fairness: if many small orgs spike, they shouldn't starve a mid-size org. fairshare or weight by contract?
kevin: propose weights by committed qps then fairshare ties for uncommitted capacity. here's a config sketch:

```
policy:
  org_limit:
    rpm: 60000   # requests/min
    tpm: 120000  # tokens/min (sum of token costs)
    concurrency: 40
  burst:
    bucket_size: 200
    refill_per_sec: 3.3
  weights:
    committed_qps: 100
    fairshare_enabled: true
```

tara: small nit: rpm/tpm units need to be surfaced in API and console. docs need example computations for embeddings vs chat.
jen: +1. Also add a rollout path: default enforcement off for 1% sample orgs, then ramp to 100% with canary metric: "throttle_rate" and "failed_requests_due_to_concurrency".
maria: telemetry: we need token-level breakdown per org and route, plus alerts when burst bucket depletion rate > 5%/min.
infra-bot: will emit metrics: org.rpm, org.tpm, org.concurrency.in_flight, org.burst.bucket_remaining.
alex: edge case: long-lived streaming connections consume concurrency but low RPM. do we want separate streaming concurrency count?
kevin: yes, separate counter for streaming-sessions so streaming apps don't get killed by bursty text api consumers. treat streaming concurrency with a different budget.
jen: UX: add inline help text "streaming connections consume X concurrency units" and a link to cost calc.
maria: opinions on enforcement order? check concurrency first, then token bucket, then RPM sliding window — to minimize head-of-line blocking.
kevin: that ordering makes sense. doc that and add a fallback: if RPM exceeded, route to cheaper model variant if available.
tara: can we add a developer-mode header to bypass strict throttles for internal test orgs? only allowed from certain IP ranges.
kevin: yes, internal bypass via API key allowlist + audit log. no bypass for public keys.
jen: action items: 1) eng-platform: prototype enforcement order + metrics (alex, tara) 2) console: display bucket + rollout toggle (jen) 3) docs: units/examples (maria) 4) infra: metric names + emitter (infra-bot assigned)
alex: I'll start a small PoC for edge vs router enforcement tradeoffs.
maria: I'll draft docs with embedding/token examples.
kevin: thanks all. will formalize into RFC next week and attach example configs. :thumbsup:
